title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 9/10: "We'll learn from it and hopefully be better for it"
headline: A.J. Brown left the opener with a possible high ankle sprain, is undergoing more tests and may miss next week; Corey Kiner stepped in at RB with TreVeyon Henderson out.
summary: Vrabel said A.J. Brown could not finish the opener. He did not confirm a high ankle sprain, saying more tests are coming and an update will follow next week. He added that he doesn't know whether Brown will be available for the next game. Morgan Moses, Hunter Henry and Carlton Davis all returned to the game after getting hurt, and Vrabel expects only bumps and bruises from them. Vrabel defended the decision to rely on joint practices rather than preseason snaps. He took responsibility for the poor execution and the second-half collapse, and said the line-of-scrimmage penalties and operation gave the team a chance early. On the final drive, he explained that Drake Maye had to throw it away because the timing and protection weren't there. He said Maye will learn from it and that he expects him to keep playing at a very high level. Vrabel said Romeo Doubs simply dropped a ball and it was not a decision error. He called Gabe Jacas' game an improvement and praised his instinctive red-zone play. He said Corey Kiner worked hard on protections and terminology but that the team must block better for him. Vrabel said the run game was better in the second half.

injuries.detail: Left the game and could not finish. Reported high ankle sprain not confirmed. More tests are pending and his availability for next week is uncertain.
Returned to the game after getting hurt; only a bump or bruise expected.

signals.note: A WR1 with a possible multi-week ankle injury is a big risk, and the pass-catching targets would likely be spread among the other receivers.

signals.claim: Kiner will get more opportunities to run while he acclimates to the offense, with Henderson out.
signals.note: Kiner is a possible fill-in RB if Henderson's absence continues, but the run blocking was poor and Vrabel's praise was mild.
signals.quote: we have to, you know, be able to give him some opportunities to, to run.

signals.claim: Maye will bounce back and continue playing at a very high level.
signals.note: Vrabel shows full confidence in Maye despite the late throw and turnover issues, so there is no concern about his role.
signals.quote: we've seen Drake perform at a, at an extremely high level.

signals.claim: Doubs' miss was a drop, not a route or decision problem.
signals.note: Vrabel doesn't think the drop signals a role issue, so Doubs' volume should hold.
signals.quote: He just, you know, he dropped the ball. That's what happens in this league.

signals.claim: Jacas continues to improve and is playing an active role on defense.
signals.note: IDP managers should note his growing role, with a tackle for loss and good run defense.
signals.quote: I thought it was, continues to improve.

topics.detail: Vrabel said the team aimed to be aggressive near field-goal range with a tie available, and that the final throw wasn't there. The team converted two fourth downs on that drive but did not execute at the end.

Early-down runs struggled, but the team ran better in the second half. Vrabel said that helped protect the offensive line and avoid a pure drop-back game, and that pass protection improved but wasn't perfect.

topics.topic: Ball security and Marcus Jones' punt returns
topics.detail: Vrabel stressed practice-based ball security and staying aggressive without being reckless. He said he trusts Marcus Jones' decisions on punts and wants to get him going in the return game.
Vrabel said missed tackles and poor communication allowed explosive plays, including a touchdown after a fourth-and-one stop attempt, and that the defense didn't make the opponent earn it.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 9/9: “We never accept losing, but we have to embrace moving on"
headline: Patriots fall in Week 1 at Seattle after Drake Maye throws three interceptions; Vrabel backs Maye, and an unnamed player's injury remains without an update.
summary: Vrabel said the Patriots failed to win the second half, pointing to turnovers and a lack of plays in critical situations. He praised the offense for battling back with fourth-down conversions but said the team has to be aggressive without being reckless. On the late interceptions, he said Maye may have tried to do too much and that the team forced some long-yardage situations. He expressed full confidence in Maye, saying the loss isn't about one player. He had no update on a player who did not return from injury, and the transcript doesn't name him. Vrabel said Seattle's run defense, ranked second in the league last year, made it hard to run, though he saw some positive runs and thought protection and balance were adequate. He said the offense handled Seattle's blitzes, including blitz zeros, mostly okay. He criticized the defense for missed tackles and for selling out against the run on a fourth-down play that went for a big gain. He also noted a punt-team penalty and one other false start, but felt the team handled the road environment well.

injuries.detail: Asked 'How is he doing?'; Vrabel said he had no update and the player wasn't able to return. The player's name isn't clear from the captions.

signals.claim: Maye remains the starting QB and the team backs him, but he must cut down on turnovers and forced throws.
signals.note: Three interceptions in a loss raise short-term turnover risk, but the coach publicly backs him and no benching is implied.
signals.quote: we have nothing but the utmost confidence in him and everybody on this football team

topics.detail: The Patriots did not make enough plays in the second half. Three interceptions and a lack of takeaways were the key issues, and Vrabel called it a broken record.
Seattle's run defense was ranked second last year. New England had some decent runs and some negative ones, but nothing good enough, though pass protection and balance held up reasonably well.
Missed tackles and selling out against the run led to a 50-yard gain on fourth down, even though the defense got stops earlier.
Seattle brought extra pressure, including blitz zeros and double-A-gap looks, but New England mostly held up and hit one big play down the field.
A punt-team penalty and one other false start occurred, but Vrabel felt the team handled the road environment well overall.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Recaps The Week 1 Win vs. Patriots
headline: Sam Darnold has a hip-area muscle injury with no new update, so Drew Lock is the fallback after a strong relief outing, and Rodney Thomas II stepped into the secondary with Ty Okada out.
summary: Macdonald said there was no new update on Darnold beyond earlier positive news. The team is still working out the extent of the injury and a plan, and he expects a clearer picture when work resumes Monday. He described it as a muscle issue around the hip area, and Darnold was back in the building. Macdonald praised Drew Lock for never putting the ball in jeopardy and for preparing like a starter, and said he expects the same if Lock plays again. He is excited about the run game, citing physical, decisive runners and fewer negative runs, and singled out Jadarian Price's first NFL action. He also highlighted Jalen Sundell, Nehemiah Pritchett, Julian Love (best game as a Seahawk) and Byron Murphy, plus DeMarcus Lawrence's play on the last interception. The seven pre-snap penalties had no single cause, so the fix is a return to fundamentals in practice, calls, motions and shifts. In the secondary, Rodney Thomas II played well with Ty Okada out and AJ Finley is ready if needed. Trevon Diggs was inactive, and Macdonald only said 'we'll see' on his availability.

injuries.detail: Muscle injury around the hip area; no new update, back in the building, and the team is still determining the extent and a plan, with more clarity expected Monday.
Missed Week 1; Macdonald said 'we'll see how long' he is out, with no timeline given.
Inactive in Week 1; asked whether he is close to playing, Macdonald only said 'we'll see.'

signals.quote: Credit to Rodney for staying ready.

signals.note: Okada's absence opened the door for Thomas, and his return timeline is unknown.

signals.note: He is a depth option if Okada's absence continues.

His pressure and cut-block hurdle set up the game-ending interception, which is good for IDP value.

signals.quote: Jobe was great earlier in the play.

signals.note: He had his first interception and good tackling, which makes him a notable secondary performer.

topics.detail: The seven pre-snap penalties had multiple small causes rather than one theme. The team will go back to the fundamentals of practice, getting calls in, and motion and shifts, without panicking.
Macdonald is excited about the run game, citing runners who were decisive, a line that ran off the ball and fewer negative runs. He said keeping drives alive would give more chances to run.
The offense has different play calls and language but is still the Seahawk offense, with physical line and tight end play and decisive receivers. Macdonald stressed clear directives for the players.
Asked whether a back earned more carries, Macdonald said usage follows how the game plays out and will be taken game by game.
Asked why the team didn't go with AJ on the fourth-and-one that led to the touchdown pass, Macdonald said they simply felt it was the best play and gave no further detail.

The defense tackled well after a preseason without live reps, though Macdonald thought they missed four to six tackles. He praised the punter's kicks for shifting field position and holding a dangerous returner to no return yards.
Opponents' systems have changed a lot from last year and teams haven't shown their identity yet. Macdonald expects the first quarter of the season to focus on improving the team's own phases.
